claims.text: The legendary figure of Lady Richeldis de Faverches, an Anglo-Saxon noblewoman, is said to have received a vision of the Virgin Mary in 1061, leading to the establishment of Walsingham as a pilgrimage site.

This vision, among the earliest recorded Marian apparitions in England, connected Walsingham to the sacred mystery of the Annunciation and reverberates through the centuries, echoing in the spirit of the stained glass here.
